implementation: fold_stream keeps FinishReason; SupervisedModel::step issues up to continue_on_length continuation requests carrying the partial output, stitches one assistant message, appends model.continued {continuation_of, index} per continuation and decrements the budget per request; status shown in exec output and the TUI.
reasoning_summary setting for dialects that support it.
validation: Stubbed provider: length twice then stop → one message, three ledger events, three budget decrements; continue_on_length = 0 leaves today's behaviour byte-identical (transcript diff).

tasks.title: Model-configuration and getting-started documentation
implementation: Document the full [model.<id>] key set, [models] fallback, [phases], keychain, presets, setup, doctor --live; correct the keyless-header, exit-code and doctor-exit claims; remove the peer-product name from the H1 and prose (rule 2.4).
validation: A test pins the documented key list to user_config's known list and the exit-code table to JsonlExitCode::ALL.

tasks.title: Durable job projection everywhere: session-scoped registry for daemon/ACP, detached completion, orphan reconciliation, job events in ACP and JSONL
implementation: Daemon/ACP sessions own one JobRegistry for the session's lifetime instead of one per turn (disclosed behaviour change: jobs survive turns there as they do in the TUI).

Detached task_spawn emits finished; job.orphan_reconciled gets its first producer from process_supervisor::reconcile_orphans at session open; ACP session/update carries job.*; rapid exec --jsonl streams job.* records.
validation: Kill the client, reconnect through the daemon, fold the events: rows identical to the pre-kill TUI rows; a detached child's row reaches a terminal state; a job whose process died between runs is orphan_reconciled; JSONL and TUI carry the same job events for one scripted run.

tasks.title: Demote a running command: keybinding and /jobs bg
implementation: A running shell_exec can be demoted (TUI key and /jobs bg <id>): the turn stops waiting, the process keeps running, completion wakes the turn through drain_notifications; the transition is a job.* event.
validation: Demote keeps the process alive and ends the turn; completion appears in the next model step; the ledger shows the transition.

tasks.title: /loop and `rapid loop add|list|rm` over PromptCron with lifetime, cap, recorded notifications
implementation: A poller inside the session loop fires due PromptCron rows as background Plan-mode turns with bounded context; rows carry a 7-day default lifetime and the store refuses the 51st active loop with a typed error; results land as notification.recorded events (the notice list becomes a projection) and never in the foreground transcript; /jobs shows next fire and expiry; deletable from the panel.
validation: A loop fires on schedule in a test with a scripted model; its output is absent from the transcript; expiry removes it; the cap test refuses the 51st.

tasks.title: `monitor` tool: per-line provenance-tagged notifications, flood control, persistence, kill
implementation: A monitor runs a command through the job path and turns each stdout line into a bounded, fenced notification.recorded; above a rate it stops itself with a notice and a hint; persistent: true lives for the session; /jobs cancel stops it.
validation: One notification per line with provenance; a flood auto-stops; a persistent monitor survives a turn boundary and stops on cancel; Windows runs the same test through crates/test-fixtures.

tasks.title: Resume summary derived from non-terminal work; wait ceilings reported as still running
implementation: On /resume and rapid exec --continue, derive a jobs/running block from job.*, agent.* and loop rows and inject it through host::build_packet_with; nothing stored separately.
Output/completion waits get job.wait_ceiling (default one hour); a timeout is reported as still running, not failure.
validation: Restart with a background process alive yields the block; with nothing running, no block (compiled-context test); a wait past the ceiling reports still running.

tasks.title: Role overlays on the spawn path: definitions gain fields, `type` resolves through agent_defs, user-level directory
implementation: AgentDefinition gains base_role, instructions, model, reasoning_effort, inputs, outputs (closed schema, narrow-only validation unchanged); ~/.rapidlm/agents/ loads below the project directory and cannot shadow builtins; LiveSubagentRunner resolves task_spawn `type` through full_inventory and applies role, tool surface, model, effort and instructions; unknown type is a typed refusal (ADR 0023 §5).
validation: An overlay requesting a tool outside its base role is rejected with field-level remediation; a valid overlay appears in /agents and rapid agents list and its model/effort reach the child's request (scripted model asserts).

tasks.title: Inbox: agent.mail.sent gets its first producer; interject/steer/queue delivery in the child's turn loop
implementation: Append agent.mail.sent before enqueue; the turn loop consults a MessageSource at the wait (interject pre-empts), at the step boundary (steer) and after completion (queue); agent.mail.delivered records where; the transcript labels the mode (ADR 0023 §1–2).
validation: Three tests prove when the child sees each mode, its ledger event and its transcript label; an undeliverable message is agent.mail.dropped with a reason.

tasks.title: Continue a finished child as a superseding turn in its lineage
implementation: A message to a terminal child starts a new runner turn for the same AgentId seeded with its recorded history plus the message; agent.state_changed {continued_from} carries the lineage; under the graph it is a superseding revision (ADR 0023 §3).
validation: Messaging a completed child continues it; the original report is unchanged; the lineage is visible in /agents.

tasks.title: Admission: bounded FIFO in SubagentRegistry with a managed, narrow-only concurrency ceiling
implementation: Spawns above the ceiling wait in order for a slot (queued position visible in the tool result and /agents) bounded by the turn ceiling; managed.max_concurrent_subagents narrows the built-in; the per-turn spawn budget is unchanged (ADR 0023 §4).
validation: Spawning twice the ceiling queues in order without error; a managed ceiling cannot be exceeded by user or project configuration (gate test).

tasks.title: Declared outputs checked at completion; subagent wait ceiling
implementation: A declared output missing from the child's result is SubagentEnd::IntegrationFailed { missing_outputs }; detached children get subagent.wait_ceiling (default one hour), expiry reported as still running (ADR 0023 §6–7).
validation: A missing declared output is a typed failure, never accepted; a wait past the ceiling reports still running and leaves the child alive.

tasks.title: Plan mode is the lattice mode: /plan, rapid exec --plan, the plan-file carve-out, the proposal type and fixture
implementation: /plan and --plan set PermissionMode::Plan as the effective mode under the managed ceiling; the lattice gains the .rapidlm/plans/ carve-out so ExecTools.plan_mode becomes a projection; add protocol::plan::PlanProposal v1 with a fixture (ADR 0024 §1–2).
validation: A write call in plan mode is refused by PermissionLattice::evaluate (policy-layer test, not prompt); the proposal fixture round-trips; the cron path's forced Plan mode is unchanged.

tasks.title: Proposal submission through the approval wait; revisions; rejection; headless exit
implementation: plan_exit stores the proposal artifact, renders .rapidlm/plans/<id>.md, appends plan.proposed and raises the approval request; edit before approval appends plan.revised {supersedes} and leaves the previous artifact intact; reject appends plan.rejected {reason}; headless --plan prints the proposal and exits NeedsApproval (ADR 0024 §3–4, §6).
validation: Editing creates a new revision and the old file/artifact are byte-identical; headless exits 10 with the proposal printed; a restart mid-wait recovers the pending approval.

tasks.title: Approval compiles the proposal into a verified run whose nodes and edges match the plan
implementation: plan.approved writes the steps as a PlaybookFile and starts rapid run --orchestration verified over it; the payload carries plan_id, revision, run_id, graph_id (ADR 0024 §5).
validation: Graph nodes and DependsOn edges equal the plan's steps and depends_on; the ledger links plan revision → run → nodes; approving a superseded revision is a typed refusal.

tasks.title: Signed managed policy (require_signature, detached signature, doctor origin/signature state)
implementation: Blocked on decision D-1 (baseline §5): the workspace has no asymmetric-signature primitive. On (a): add the Ed25519 verifier in crates/security, managed.trusted_keys, <policy>.sig, fail-closed refusal before session start; reuse the verifier for the update manifest's documented signatures.
validation: An unsigned or invalid policy under require_signature is refused before a session starts with remediation; a valid signature loads; doctor shows origin and signature state.
evidence: decision needed — see docs/goals/seams-phase0-baseline-2026-09-20.md §5 D-1

tasks.title: MCP and plugin-source allow/deny lists enforced before any write; trust gate on mcp add
implementation: managed.mcp.allowed_servers/denied_servers (name and command/URL pattern) and managed.plugins.allowed_sources enforced at mcp add, plugin install and session bind with the field/origin/remediation report; mcp add gains the trust gate it lacks (disclosed: an untrusted project's add becomes a refusal that writes nothing); mcp probe and doctor list what policy blocks.
validation: mcp add of a denied server writes nothing (directory hash unchanged) and reports the gate; a denied plugin source likewise; an untrusted project's add is refused.

tasks.title: Deterministic tool-name collision rule and User-Agent on MCP HTTP and provider calls
implementation: Surface assembly reports a collision once (built-in > plugin > MCP), keeps the namespaced mcp__<server>__<tool> reachable and dedups identical names; write_http_request and the MCP transport send User-Agent: rapid/<version>.
validation: A tool present built-in and via MCP resolves to the built-in and stays reachable under the namespace; the header appears on both writers (scripted server asserts).

tasks.title: Installer by shape: rapid mcp install --into/--discover with format-preserving edits
implementation: --into <path> [--format jsonc|toml|yaml] [--key <path>] [--dry-run]: format-preserving edit (comments, ordering, unrelated keys untouched), timestamped .bak, atomic 0600 write, per-user lock, unchanged on repeat, diff on dry-run; --discover scans the home/XDG roots (overridable by environment) for files whose shape declares a servers map under a small set of known key names and lists them by path (rule 2.5).
validation: Fixture files: the byte diff is limited to the injected block; .bak written; unchanged on the second run; nothing written under --dry-run; --discover finds neutral-named fixtures by shape only; a concurrent run is refused by the lock.

tasks.title: Skill package teaching external hosts to drive rapid headlessly, with a --help drift test
implementation: skill/SKILL.md (open skill format): agent-mode flags, stdout/stderr contract, exit codes, JSONL, resume rules, key handling; a sub-skill for long-running goals.
validation: A test extracts every command line from the package and runs it against --help; no documented flag can drift.

tasks.title: Cost in the ledger, then rapid usage and /usage derived from it
implementation: model.completed gains input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_tokens and cost: AccountedCost additively; rapid usage [<session>] [--project] [--since] [--output json] [--quiet] reduces model.* events per turn with totals and TSV; reported vs estimated flagged; /usage beside /context in one tabbed modal whose context legend sums to 100%.
validation: usage totals equal the sum of the fixture session's ledger records; estimated vs reported flagged; a pre-change ledger reduces with cost unknown, never zero.

tasks.title: rapid du with a reclaim plan that never deletes
implementation: Sizes of the per-project .rapidlm tree (sessions, index, findings, runs, plans), RAPIDLM_HOME and the worktree store; --reclaim-plan lists only entries SEAM-08's rule would reclaim; the layout printed is the real one (baseline §3 SEAM-07).
validation: du matches the filesystem for a fixture home/project within block rounding; the reclaim plan equals reclaim --dry-run.

tasks.title: [ui.status_line]: builtin | command | disabled with a schema-versioned payload run under the sandbox
implementation: type, items, command, refresh_interval (1–86400 s); protocol::status::StatusPayload v1 with fixture on stdin (session_id, model, effort, context.used_percent, cost, goal.state, worktree, workspace.cwd/repo, trigger); runs through run_sandboxed with a timeout; up to five lines cut at 1024 chars; last output retained on failure; a project-level command requires trust; RAPIDLM_SESSION_ID/RAPIDLM_TURN_ID exported.
validation: Runs sandboxed; times out to the last output; honours refresh_interval; payload validates against the fixture; an untrusted project's command does not run; typed unavailability where the sandbox tier is absent.

tasks.title: Opt-in OTLP exporter through egress policy with a receipt
implementation: [telemetry.otlp] endpoint (disabled by default) gives crates/telemetry its first dependent and a real OtlpTransport behind EgressProxy with record_egress; redaction first; bounded queue; loss never a caller-visible failure.
validation: Disabled by default (no socket opened); only redacted records leave (scripted collector asserts); an egress receipt is recorded; a dead collector never fails the turn.

tasks.title: rapid exec --worktree and rapid goal create --worktree over GitWorktreeStore; base reuse without network
implementation: Decision D-2 recorded (recommendation: keep the store's in-repo location); --worktree [<name>] creates a view through GitWorktreeStore::create_view and roots the run's tools there; the worktree metadata gains session id; branch-tip fetch default, --full-history opt-in.
validation: Headless --worktree leaves the primary tree's git status unchanged; base reuse creates the linked worktree with the network unreachable (proxy variables pointed at a closed port).

tasks.title: Reclaim rule over the journal; rapid worktree list|reclaim [--dry-run]; journaled abandon
implementation: A worktree is reclaimable only when its transaction is published or abandoned in the journal, no active lease/session references it and git status is clean; abandon is journaled as a workspace.abandon effect; the primary checkout is never a candidate; --dry-run lists without deleting; reclaim records the removal.
validation: Reclaim refuses unpublished changes or an active lease; dry-run deletes nothing; a published worktree is reclaimed and the journal records it.

tasks.title: Persisted never-allow and always-allow answers with origin in permissions list
implementation: Approval prompts offer never/always for MCP tools and fetch domains; deny grants persisted per project beside allow grants; permissions list shows every effective rule with its origin (persisted, settings, managed); ACP allow_always persists too.
validation: A persisted never-allow blocks without prompting on the next run and appears with origin; revert cycle.

tasks.title: AST-aware shell matcher on security::tokenize_shell; safe-command list in auto mode
implementation: Rules match the parsed script (quoted variables, pipelines, ;/&&, subshells, heredocs) so quoting neither bypasses nor over-prompts; unknown constructs prompt; auto mode allows a fixed safe list (directory creation, touch, listing).
validation: Matcher fixtures per construct produce the expected decision; a quoting bypass fixture is denied; the safe list is allowed only in auto.

tasks.title: rapid exec --allow <rule> bounded by the managed ceiling; default mode in user config
implementation: Repeatable --allow adds startup grants for the run, narrowed by max_permission_mode/denied_tools; [permissions] default_mode in user config below managed and above project settings.
validation: --allow cannot exceed the managed ceiling (gate test); the user default is honoured and overridden by env.

tasks.title: Prompts render the full script and the file-edit diff via the existing view model
implementation: paint_screen renders tui::ApprovalViewModel (already exported and snapshot-tested) for pending approvals: full script for shell, auto-expanded diff for edits.
validation: Snapshot test of the production modal shows diff and script; the old three-line snapshot is replaced, not weakened.

tasks.title: Agent-mode flags parsed once, env mirrors, JSON error envelope with hints, headless origin tag
implementation: --output json|text, --quiet, --non-interactive, --dry-run, --yes, --no-color, --timeout with RAPIDLM_* mirrors parsed before dispatch; non-TTY stdout defaults to JSON where a JSON form exists; protocol::cli::CliError {code, message, hint} with fixture rendered as {"error":{…}} on stderr in JSON mode; every InteractiveError gains a hint naming the next command; session.created gains origin = headless|interactive; sessions list --origin.
Candidate recorded by SEAM-01-2: a headless `rapid approvals list|approve|deny <session> <n>` so a parked exec turn can be resolved without the TUI (today: `rapid resume <session>` then /approvals).
validation: Table-driven test over every subcommand; envelope fixture; exit codes unchanged (pinned); sessions list --origin filters.

tasks.title: MCP elicitation and form/URL consent through the approval wait, durable across restart
implementation: A tool result with an input-required state and schema raises the approval wait (source mcp:<server>); the answer is carried on the retried call; server-initiated elicitation frames are surfaced, not discarded.
validation: Round trip against a stub server; a restart mid-elicitation resumes; an invalid answer is a typed refusal.

tasks.title: web_search behind a backend trait with domain lists, bounded, provenance-tagged, egress under policy
implementation: [toolset.web_search] backend, allowed_domains, excluded_domains; results fenced and bounded; egress through EgressProxy with a receipt; web_fetch gains the same receipt while there; no backend configured is typed unavailability.
validation: Results filtered by the domain lists (stub backend); no backend → typed unavailability; receipts recorded.

tasks.title: RAPIDLM_SESSION_ID/RAPIDLM_TURN_ID exported; /aside as a read-only child whose answer never enters the context
implementation: Export both variables at the tool, hook, MCP and status-command spawn sites; /aside <question> runs a read-only child with no inbox and shows the answer without appending it.
validation: Each spawn site receives the variables; the aside's content is provably absent from the next turn's compiled context.

tasks.title: Resume recap, /rename [--auto], prompt stash, /edit-prompt
implementation: A host-generated recap (last-turn summary, durations, unmet criteria) derived at resume; session.renamed event with the title as a projection; a stash keybinding; /edit-prompt in $EDITOR.
validation: One test per item; the recap is derived (no stored copy).

tasks.title: /memory flush: typed records with evidence links into the memory store and the MEMORY.md projection
implementation: context_engine::memory::MemoryStore gets its first production caller; flush writes decisions/patterns with provenance and evidence links; MEMORY.md is regenerated as a projection.
validation: Flush writes typed records with provenance; MEMORY.md reflects them; revert cycle.

tasks.title: /memory consolidate as a scheduled loop producing new revisions with provenance
implementation: A PromptCron-backed loop folds context.compacted summaries into topic notes as new revisions; sources are never destroyed; the run is visible in /jobs.
validation: Consolidation produces a new revision, sources intact; the job appears in /jobs.

tasks.title: Passive update notice: opt-in, TTY-only, throttled, budgeted, receipted
implementation: Decision D-3 recorded (recommendation: [update] url, no built-in default); [update] check = true; skipped in CI, non-TTY and headless; at most once per 24 h with a 3 s timeout; state file under RAPIDLM_HOME; one line at exit; egress through the proxy with a receipt.
validation: Throttling, CI skip, no hang without network (closed port), receipt recorded.

tasks.title: Agent dashboard as a daemon-hosted projection
implementation: A cross-session overview (sessions, forks, loops, pinned agents, last-turn summary, new-agent action) reduced from ledger events by the daemon; nothing stored separately.
validation: Every row is derivable from the ledger; killing and restarting the daemon reproduces the dashboard byte-for-byte.

phase_notes.note: Phase 0 complete: baseline audit with fifteen item rechecks (eleven 'today' corrections, none widening the program), ADRs 0022–0024, this worklist, the SEAMS section of the development ledger. Three decisions recorded (D-1 signature primitive, D-2 worktree location, D-3 update URL); only SEAM-06-1 is blocked on one of them.

SEAM-01-1 landed: protocol::hooks::HookResult (rapidlm.hook_result v2) with fixture; the hook runner separates stdout (result) from stderr (detail); allow/deny/defer applied at the one dispatch site, every v2 decision recorded as hook.decided (rapidlm.hook.decision/v1) through a HookEvents sink attached with the other ledger sinks and propagated to subagent children; `ask` is an explicit, recorded denial until SEAM-01-2 routes it onto the approval wait. v1 hooks are byte-identical and record nothing.

SEAM-01-2 landed: a hook `ask` is the existing approval wait (ApprovalRequest/approval.requested gain an additive `source`), the approved resume runs the call once without re-asking, a hook deny still denies on resume; headless exec installs a hook-only ledger sink, records the suspension like the TUI and exits NeedsApproval (10) naming `rapid resume` as the next command, while a permission Ask keeps its typed denial.

SEAM-01-3 landed: a hook's updated_input replaces the call once it passes ProposedToolCall bounds, the tool's own argument parser and the permission lattice (evaluated on the rewritten call — a rewrite cannot widen policy); hook.input_rewritten carries both inputs and digests before anything runs; the model's result and the TUI transcript both carry a one-line marker; the last rewriting hook wins, a deny discards, an ask shows the human the rewritten call.

SEAM-01-4 landed: pre and post hooks' additional_context follows the tool result inside the <untrusted_context locator="hook:…"> fence, bounded at 4 KiB and redacted like the result; post hooks gain the v2 contract (context delivered, decision recorded, cannot block); a denial delivers none.

SEAM-01-5 landed: user_prompt_submit (blocks with a reason; TUI restores the composer; a blocked queued message is held and survives a restart; headless exits 3), stop / stop_cancelled exclusive at the three turn-end sites with the stop reason, subagent_stop deny blocks the child's completion (inline and detached — the detached path now fires the subagent hooks), post_tool_use_failure adds context after a failure; observing stages fail open with hook.failed recorded.
